proficiencyLevelDescriptionOne: We aim to diagnose children's skill levels as early as possible, to promptly group them based on their proficiency, allowing them to develop their language skills at their own pace and make the most of lessons. As every year, a diagnosis of the language proficiency of our students was conducted according to the European Language Education System using mock Cambridge exams.
proficiencyLevelDescriptionTwo: Cambridge tests for children are comprehensive and diagnostic - they cannot be failed; they are designed to indicate the level of language proficiency. Percentages are crucial. We consider that a student has reached a certain proficiency level if they achieve a minimum of 60%. However, to confirm that a student has genuinely attained a particular language level and can take the official Cambridge exam, they should score around 80% in mock tests. In the mock tests, we assess listening, reading, and writing skills. Speaking is also included in the actual exam, which we practice and evaluate regularly.
additionalExamInfoFirst: BRITANNIA is an authorized Cambridge Preparation Centre, so our students take exams on-site at the school every year. Students can take exams with us at all proficiency levels.
additionalExamInfoSecond: Exam session in Britannia is organized in June.
additionalExamInfoThird: The experience of taking a real exam and its atmosphere is incredibly valuable. It mentally prepares children for taking subsequent important exams, builds resilience to stress, and boosts self-esteem. It provides children with a lot of motivation to learn, and after receiving a certificate from England at our significant ceremony, it also gives them a great sense of satisfaction and a desire to further improve their skills. Children truly feel distinguished.
additionalExamInfoFourth: Above all, it is also the most credible confirmation of acquired language skills. Results and certificates are sent from England. The approach to the exam should be a reward and motivation for the child. Participation is not mandatory.
additionalExamInfoFifth: The payment is for the examination centre, not for us. We are guides on the journey to your child's success.
learningMode.firstParagraph: The year-round work of the student, their commitment, mastery of the material, results of ongoing tests, and diagnostic mock exams are important to us and serve as the basis for qualification into groups with similar language competencies in the next school year. We also consider individual abilities and the level of student motivation throughout the entire school year.
learningMode.secondParagraph: We strive to maximize support for the language potential of students and group children according to their abilities. Whenever possible, we create three types of courses:
learningMode.list.firstElement: BFT, which stands for BRITANNIA Fast Track – for outstanding students with results of 90% and above, demonstrating fluency in communication, actively utilizing learned content, being open and highly engaged in learning, regularly and at a faster pace progressing through subsequent Cambridge exams. Often, this group includes children who participate in language competitions in subsequent years or choose bilingual profiles in high school. BFT groups are usually not transported groups; they consist of children from different classes and schools.
learningMode.list.secondElement: BRT, which stands for BRITANNIA Regular Track – for students who have mastered the material very well and well, are always prepared, and are willing and motivated to use English and achieve the best results; they are eager to become proficient in English. Students in this group typically regularly take subsequent Cambridge exams.
learningMode.list.thirdElement: BST, which stands for BRITANNIA Support Track – for students achieving results below 65% and those who need more support in mastering the material, are hesitant in speaking activation, and need to open up more to learning.
recommendationToCambridgeExam: Based on the December diagnostic assessment, we provide a preliminary recommendation for taking the Cambridge exam at the end of the school year.
